60169702.s: The Dancing Fountain is one of Najran's best-known entertainment landmarks, in King Saud Park in the Al Fahd district. It puts on colourful water shows set to music, in a park with space for strolling and walking.
60169702.b:
The Dancing Fountain is one of Najran's best-known entertainment landmarks, in King Saud Park in the Al Fahd district. It consists of water rings around a main ring from which water shoots high in colourful shows set to music.

The fountain is surrounded by a park with space for strolling and walking, play areas and cafés, making it a favourite destination for families and visitors in the evenings.

60169690.s: "Lil Madi Athar" is a private heritage museum in Rafha Governorate in the Northern Borders region. It was founded by local resident Sayyah Qasim Al Shammari after many years of collecting rare pieces since childhood, and it welcomes both locals and tourists.
60169690.b:
"Lil Madi Athar" is a private heritage museum in Rafha Governorate in the Northern Borders region. It was founded by local resident Sayyah Qasim Al Shammari after many years of collecting rare pieces since childhood, and it welcomes both locals and tourists.

The museum holds thousands of varied items, including old weapons, swords and shields, pottery and handicrafts, coins and traditional costumes, as well as old cars and devices and exhibits documenting how life has developed in the Kingdom, and the "amariyah", the litter once carried on camels' backs. The museum reflects the heritage of the Northern Borders in particular and of the Arabian Peninsula in general.

60169687.s: Al-Jumaimah is one of the stations on the Zubaydah Trail. It is now in Saudi Arabia, in the Northern Borders region near the Iraqi border. The site has a pool known as Al Juraisi Pool or Al-Jumaimah Pool, as well as the ruins of a palace with a row of shops and another building.
60169687.b: Al-Jumaimah is one of the stations on the Zubaydah Trail. It is now in Saudi Arabia, in the Northern Borders region near the Iraqi border. The site has a pool known as Al Juraisi Pool or Al-Jumaimah Pool, as well as the ruins of a palace with a row of shops and another building.

60169620.s: Zubala is a village in Rafha Governorate in the Northern Borders region of Saudi Arabia. It contains a historic site and is known as one of the stations on the Zubaydah Trail. It lies south of Rafha, 25 km away, on the old pilgrim road, with ancient remains, pools and wells that collect water from Wadi Al Manashbi, Aba Al Rumam and Umm Usafir. It was once a stop for pilgrims and travellers, and is now home to the Al Sulait clan of Al Yahya of the Shammar tribe.

60169575.s: Linah is a village in northern Najd in Saudi Arabia, one of the oldest settlements in the Arabian Peninsula and a station on the Zubaydah Trail used by Iraqi pilgrims. Linah has long been known for its sweet water and its many wells, about 300 in all. Its historic landmarks include King Abdulaziz's Palace, built in 1354 AH, and the old "Al Mushahada" souq, named after the Iraqi Mushahada traders who came to the market to trade with the people of Najd.

60169570.s: Arar National Park is one of the main natural green spaces for families in Arar, with lawns, walking paths, cycle tracks and family seating areas.
60169570.b:
Arar National Park is one of the main natural green spaces for families in Arar. It lies on the edge of the city and offers wide spaces to relax away from the bustle of the neighbourhoods.

The park has lawns, gardens, walking paths and cycle tracks, along with areas for exercise and family seating. Locals visit especially in spring and when the weather is mild, to enjoy the outdoors and spend time with family.

60169507.s: Bassam Al-Mefleh Personal Museum is one of the private museums in Arar, part of a group of community museums in the Northern Borders region founded by heritage collectors to document the region's history and connect new generations with the lives of their forebears.
60169507.b:
Bassam Al-Mefleh Personal Museum is one of the private museums in Arar, part of a group of community museums in the Northern Borders region founded by heritage collectors to document the region's history and connect new generations with the lives of their forebears.

The museum displays heritage items collected by its owner that reflect traditional life in the north of the Kingdom, and it makes a good stop for lovers of heritage and local history while visiting Arar.

60169505.s: Agran Mountain is near the Duqrah area, an archaeological site 40 km northwest of Turaif Governorate in the Northern Borders region. The site dates to the late Roman period or the early Islamic period, and some researchers believe the ruins of the buildings at Duqrah date to the Umayyad era.

60169501.s: Boulevard Mall is a shopping and entertainment destination in Arar, bringing together fashion, footwear and accessories stores along with a variety of restaurants and cafés suited to families.
60169501.b:
Boulevard Mall is a shopping and entertainment destination in Arar, bringing together under one roof a range of stores specialising in men's, women's and children's fashion, footwear and bags, and accessories and gifts, along with a number of well-known brands.

The mall also has a variety of restaurants and cafés, and services such as car parking and ATMs, making it a good choice for families looking to combine shopping with a meal.

60169483.s: Al-Musaidiyah Park and Walkway is one of the main green destinations in Arar. It lies on the east side of the city and brings locals and families together for walking and outings.
60169483.b:
Al-Musaidiyah Park and Walkway is one of the main green destinations in Arar. It lies on the east side of the city and brings locals and families together for walking and outings.

Palm trees define the place, and walking paths run between lawns and open spaces, making it a good spot for walking, relaxing and spending time with family outdoors, especially on mild evenings.

60169391.s: Al-Dir' Quarter is a ruined neighbourhood in the middle of Dumat Al-Jandal, in the archaeological area next to Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque, in Al-Jouf Governorate in the north of Saudi Arabia.
60169391.b:
Al-Dir' Quarter is a ruined neighbourhood in the middle of Dumat Al-Jandal, in the archaeological area next to Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque, in Al-Jouf Governorate in the north of Saudi Arabia.

The quarter consists of adjoining stone houses with interconnected alleys, some covered by arches. The alleys were paved with stone in 1413 AH. Some houses have two storeys and are roofed with tamarisk wood and palm fronds. Moving around the site is dangerous because most of the houses are on the verge of collapse. Al-Dir' is one of the surviving remains of the old city of Dumat Al-Jandal, which escaped the demolition that hit the Dumat Al-Jandal souq. The quarter dates to the medieval Islamic period, but it stands on archaeological layers and foundations dating to the middle of the first millennium BC. It is distinguished by its stone arches, stone buildings and alleys, and by its setting among orchards and water channels that supplied the residents with water from nearby springs. It also stands on the ruins of earlier quarters, as the multiple layers and the old road of the quarter appearing beneath the present buildings make clear.

60169384.s: Kaf Heritage Village is an old village near Kaf Castle, 27 km from the nearest settlement. It is made up of adjoining mud houses, with palm farms scattered throughout and an old stone mosque at its centre, and it includes a school also built of stone in the old Islamic architectural style. The village has a salt flat and several flowing sulphur springs used to irrigate the palm farms, and many visitors now come for sulphur-water treatment of skin conditions. The site was chosen for tourism because of its heritage and therapeutic value and its fit with nearby tourist sites such as Kaf Castle.
60169384.b:
Kaf Heritage Village is an old village near Kaf Castle, 27 km from the nearest settlement. It is made up of adjoining mud houses, with palm farms scattered throughout and an old stone mosque at its centre, and it includes a school also built of stone in the old Islamic architectural style. The village has a salt flat and several flowing sulphur springs used to irrigate the palm farms, and many visitors now come for sulphur-water treatment of skin conditions. The site was chosen for tourism because of its heritage and therapeutic value and its fit with nearby tourist sites such as Kaf Castle and Al Saidi Castle.

At its northern edge is Al Saidi Mountain, topped by a castle dating to the Nabataean period that was later used as a garrison protecting the pilgrim route. It is built of volcanic stone, and the road leading to it is winding, with its sides paved in stone. On the northeast side of the mountain stands a large palace attributed to Sheikh Nuri Al Sha'lan, built of large blocks of sandstone.

60169373.s: Al-Dhil' is one of the oldest historic quarters in Sakaka, at the foot of the hill topped by Zaabal Castle in the northwest of the city. Together with the castle and the nearby Sisra Well, it forms a complete heritage ensemble.
60169373.b:
Al-Dhil' is one of the oldest historic quarters in Sakaka, at the foot of the hill topped by Zaabal Castle in the northwest of the city. Together with the castle and the nearby Sisra Well, it forms a complete heritage ensemble.

The quarter is known for its adjoining houses of mud and stone, built in the architectural style once common in Al-Jouf, some with two storeys, and for its many alleys, some roofed with palm fronds and tamarisk branches. The quarter has been redeveloped as one of the region's heritage destinations, and it is recommended to visit it together with Zaabal Castle to enjoy the views over Sakaka.

60169356.s: Sisra Well is one of the archaeological wells in the Al-Jouf region of Saudi Arabia. It is carved into the rock west of Zaabal Fort, with a staircase cut into the rock along one side and a rectangular opening at the bottom followed by a larger one. This confirms that the well was a source of water from the region's ancient springs.
60169356.b: Sisra Well is one of the archaeological wells in the Al-Jouf region of Saudi Arabia. It is carved into the rock west of Zaabal Fort, with a staircase cut into the rock along one side and a rectangular opening at the bottom followed by a larger one. 60169325.s: Al-Nuwaiser Heritage Museum is one of the museums of the Al-Jouf region in the north of Saudi Arabia. It is in Dumat Al-Jandal and was founded by Ali bin Nuwaiser Al-Hasan. It occupies the old emirate building next to Marid Castle and has two halls, a heritage tent, three rooms and a traditional market of seven rooms selling heritage items. The two halls display old coins, Qurans, jewellery, swords, rifles, shields, carpets, weaving tools, hospitality and Arabic coffee utensils and farming tools, as well as a complete heritage tent and three rooms with taxidermy and fossils. The traditional market displays stamps, coins and a variety of heritage and folk items.

60169305.s: Al-Jouf Amusement City is a family destination in the Al Sulaymaniyah district of Sakaka, combining children's rides and green spaces, with family seating areas, restaurants and cafés.
60169305.b:
Al-Jouf Amusement City is a family destination in the Al Sulaymaniyah district of Sakaka, combining rides for children of all ages with open green spaces.

The city has gardens and family seating areas along with restaurants, cafés and shops. It hosts entertainment events during seasons and holidays, and is a good choice for an enjoyable evening, especially in autumn and winter when the weather in Al-Jouf turns mild.

60169304.s: Al-Jouf Regional Museum of Archaeology and Folk Heritage is one of the leading museums in the north of the Kingdom. It is in Dumat Al-Jandal Governorate, close to Marid Castle, Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque and Al-Dir' Quarter, within the historic area of the old town. The exhibition hall has explanatory panels that tell the history of the Al-Jouf region in chronological order, along with archaeological finds from the region and folk heritage exhibits that reflect the lives of local people in the past. The museum is an ideal first stop for a tour of Dumat Al-Jandal's historic landmarks and for understanding their story before visiting them.
60169304.b:

60169302.s: Zaabal Castle is an archaeological fortress in Sakaka in the Al-Jouf region, on a mountaintop in the northwest of the city. It is a wall of stone and mud with four towers at its corners, reached by a single winding road. The castle protected the city for a long time because of the strength of its fortifications and the difficulty of reaching it, and locals tell legendary stories of how it stood firm against invaders who wanted to destroy it because of its strategic importance.

60169301.s: Marid Castle is a historic military fortress in Dumat Al-Jandal in the Al-Jouf region, about 50 km from Sakaka. It dates to the 1st century AD, and its oldest mention is from the 3rd century AD, when Queen Zenobia (240 - 274) invaded Dumat Al-Jandal and Tayma but could not storm the castle, and said: "Marid has rebelled, and Al-Ablaq is mighty."
60169301.b:
Marid Castle is a historic military fortress in Dumat Al-Jandal in the Al-Jouf region, about 50 km from Sakaka. It dates to the 1st century AD, and its oldest mention is from the 3rd century AD, when Queen Zenobia (240 - 274) invaded Dumat Al-Jandal and Tayma but could not storm the castle, and said: "Marid has rebelled, and Al-Ablaq is mighty."

The castle stands on a hill about 620 m above sea level and overlooks the city of Dumat Al-Jandal in Al-Jouf from the west. This helped make it a strong stronghold, since someone looking out from the castle can see every part of the town and spot anyone approaching from far away. Marid Castle was given its name because it rebelled against, and resisted, anyone who tried to storm it, as Yaqut al-Hamawi mentions.
60169301.a: King Saud Road, Al Khaldiyah, Dumat Al-Jandal

60169300.s: The Rajajil Columns are an archaeological site, the oldest in the Al-Jouf region of Saudi Arabia, in the Qarah suburb south of Sakaka. The site consists of 50 groups of upright stone columns known as the Rajajil, each group made up of three to seven columns carved from sandstone. Some of the standing columns are more than three metres tall and about 60 centimetres thick. They are called the Rajajil ("men") because from a distance they look like the figure of a man.

60169248.s: Amazon Oasis Reserve is a private tourist destination in Dumat Al-Jandal Governorate, known for its large numbers of varied ornamental birds, along with tame animals and green farmland among the palm trees.
60169248.b:
Amazon Oasis Reserve is a private tourist destination in Dumat Al-Jandal Governorate, known for its large numbers of varied ornamental birds, along with tame animals and green farmland among the palm trees.

The reserve attracts families, children, bird lovers and photographers, and offers visitors a different experience in the heart of the Dumat Al-Jandal oasis. A visit can be combined with nearby historic sights such as Marid Castle, Omar ibn Al-Khattab Mosque and Dumat Al-Jandal Lake.

60169246.s: Dumat Al-Jandal Lake is not a natural lake but an artificial one, created in Dumat Al-Jandal in the Al-Jouf region in the north of Saudi Arabia. It is considered the largest artificial lake in the Arabian Peninsula.
60169246.b:
Dumat Al-Jandal Lake is not a natural lake but an artificial one, created in Dumat Al-Jandal in the Al-Jouf region in the north of Saudi Arabia. It is considered the largest artificial lake in the Arabian Peninsula.

The lake lies east of the city of Dumat Al-Jandal and is surrounded by sand dunes and palm farms, giving it a unique scene that combines water and desert. Locals and visitors come for walks, family outings and photography, especially at sunset, and it is one of the most notable natural landmarks in Al-Jouf alongside its historic sites.

60149028.s: Umm Sinman Mountain is one of the mountains of the Hail region in the north of Saudi Arabia. It lies west of the town of Jubbah, about 100 kilometres northwest of Hail in the Nafud desert. Jubbah is one of the most important archaeological sites in the Kingdom, with inscriptions and rock art spread across Umm Sinman Mountain and the nearby mountains, dating to different periods.
60149028.b:
Umm Sinman Mountain is one of the mountains of the Hail region in the north of Saudi Arabia. It lies west of the town of Jubbah, about 100 kilometres northwest of Hail in the Nafud desert. Jubbah is one of the most important archaeological sites in the Kingdom, with inscriptions and rock art spread across Umm Sinman Mountain and the nearby mountains, dating to different periods.

The area was originally an ancient lake bed surrounded by the dunes of the Great Nafud, with sedimentary mountains rising to the west and south, the most prominent being Umm Sinman, Ghota, Shuwayhit and Unayzah. In 2015, the "Rock Art in the Hail Region" site, which includes Umm Sinman Mountain in Jubbah and the Manjor and Raat mountains in Shuwaymis, was inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List.

60149024.s: Al Eyadah Heritage Museum in Jubbah Governorate displays a collection of heritage items and tools that reflect the history of the region and the lives of earlier generations. It is one of the main museums in the Hail region and draws visitors interested in local heritage.
60149024.b: Al Eyadah Heritage Museum in Jubbah Governorate displays a collection of heritage items and tools that reflect the history of the region and the lives of earlier generations. It is one of the main museums in the Hail region and draws visitors interested in local heritage.

60149022.s: Al Naif Palace Archaeological Museum is one of the museums of the Hail region. It was founded by Saud bin Naif bin Atiq Al Ramali Al Shammari. The museum is a large ground floor divided into seven sections of different sizes, and holds approximately 2,165 pieces. The collection includes coffee utensils, old clothing, jewellery and women's adornments, sewing tools, leather goods such as waterskins and leather mats, and many copper items such as coffee pots, grinders and containers for storing drinking water, as well as a collection of weapons and war equipment.
60149022.b: Al Naif Palace Archaeological Museum is one of the museums of the Hail region. It was founded by Saud bin Naif bin Atiq Al Ramali Al Shammari. The museum is a large ground floor divided into seven sections of different sizes, and holds approximately 2,165 pieces. The collection includes coffee utensils, old clothing, jewellery and women's adornments, sewing tools, leather goods such as waterskins and leather mats, and many copper items such as coffee pots, grinders and containers for storing drinking water, as well as a collection of weapons and war equipment. The display uses glass cabinets, stands, shelves and cupboards, while heavy pieces are displayed on the floor, and items are arranged by function and material.
